title: User Feedback: Visual & UX Issues
description:
Address three critical issues from user testing:
1. Clubs and Spades are hard to distinguish visually
2. HeyHey button only works for current player + missing animation
3. Empty working pile tap creates unintended card placements

title: Improve Clubs symbol visibility
description:
The Clubs and Spades suit symbols are hard to distinguish during gameplay. Adjust the Clubs symbol design to make it more visually distinct from Spades. Consider:
- Increasing size slightly
- Adjusting shape/thickness
- Adding subtle color variation (while maintaining black)
- Testing with multiple players for clarity

Location: packages/client/src/components/Card/ or shared card rendering logic

title: Fix HeyHey button and victory animation
description:
Two related issues with the HeyHey button:

1. Button only works for the player whose 'turn' it is - this is incorrect. The HeyHey button should work for ANY player who clears their Nertz pile first, regardless of turn order.

2. Victory animation not showing - when HeyHey is pressed, the confetti animation should play FIRST, then transition to the between-rounds screen. Currently going straight to between-rounds.

Requirements:
- HeyHey button should be clickable by any player when their Nertz pile is empty
- Victory animation (confetti) must play before round end screen
- Ensure socket events properly broadcast the winner to all players

Location: packages/client/src/components/HeyHeyButton.tsx, GameScreen.tsx, packages/server/src/events/gameEvents.ts

title: Prevent cards on empty working pile tap
description:
Issue: Tapping an empty working pile can incorrectly populate cards, causing out-of-order placement. This happens in two scenarios:

1. **During Setup Phase**: Accidental double-tap on a working pile slot can place 2 cards instead of 1. Each working pile should only receive exactly 1 card during setup.

2. **During Gameplay**: Tapping an empty working pile can auto-place a card from deck/Nertz. Cards should ONLY be placed on empty working piles through explicit drag actions from the Nertz pile or deck/waste area, not by tapping the empty pile itself.

Fix Requirements:
- Setup phase: Enforce 1 card per working pile limit, ignore additional taps on already-filled slots
- Gameplay phase: Disable tap-to-place on empty working piles
- Only allow drag-and-drop for placing cards on empty working piles
- Validate the fix doesn't break normal card placement on non-empty piles

Location: packages/client/src/pages/GameScreen.tsx, useCardSelection.ts, setup state machine logic
